description: We’re a team of AI Engineering and Science students from Galala University with hands-on experience in deep learning, NLP, computer vision, and satellite imagery analysis, including fine-tuning large transformer models. We focus on shipping a working prototype fast, then iterating until it’s demo-ready.
summary:
SAFER-X is a research-support platform that makes NASA’s space combustion evidence easier to explore and understand. It brings experimental records into a searchable atlas, helps users compare conditions, maps relationships between evidence, and highlights gaps where more research is needed. Each assessment links back to its sources and clearly communicates its limitations.

The platform also includes Flame Vision, which lets users explore measurements extracted from Saffire-V footage, and a combustion simulator that visualizes modeled flame behavior under different gravity and atmospheric conditions. Simulated results are clearly distinguished from experimental measurements.

By bringing scattered evidence and visual tools together, SAFER-X helps researchers investigate how flames behave beyond Earth and identify questions that need further study. This matters as future missions will operate in environments where understanding combustion is essential to protecting crews and spacecraft.
details:
SAFER-X is a research-support platform designed to make NASA’s space combustion data easier to explore, compare, and understand. Spacecraft fire research spans many experiments, materials, and environmental conditions. SAFER-X brings these pieces together so researchers and students can investigate the evidence and see where important questions remain unanswered.

The Evidence Atlas lets users search the available corpus and examine results alongside their sources. The platform helps users compare experimental conditions, explore connections between evidence, and identify areas where coverage is limited. Evidence Passports record sources, methods, and limitations so that findings can be traced back to their origins.

Flame Vision adds an interactive way to study combustion through NASA Saffire-V footage and computer-vision overlays. Its measurements use pixels and the video’s playback clock, making their limits clear. The Combustion Simulator complements this with modeled, three-dimensional visualizations of flames under different gravity and atmospheric conditions, including illustrative Earth, ISS, Moon, and Mars scenarios.

Our creative approach combines a searchable research atlas, video analysis, and interactive simulation in one workspace. Users can move from examining experimental evidence to exploring modeled scenarios while seeing the distinction between measured and simulated results.

We developed SAFER-X with Python and FastAPI for the backend, and React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS for the web interface. We used OpenCV for video analysis, Three.js and WebGL 2 for visualization, and Cantera to support the simulator’s combustion calculations. Data tools include DuckDB and Parquet for organizing the research corpus.

Throughout development, we considered source traceability, differences between experimental conditions, missing data, and scientific uncertainty. SAFER-X is intended to support exploration and research planning; its simulations are simplified models, and the platform does not certify spacecraft fire safety. Our intended impact is to make space combustion research more accessible and help researchers identify evidence gaps relevant to future missions.
